websearch.worst: B: summary says BPA was found in all 47 samples; page says only that traces of BPA were also found
websearch.worst_summary_quote: Bisphenol A was also found in all 47 human samples.
websearch.worst_page_quote: They also found traces of bisphenol A (BPA), a material used in food containers.
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader would believe BPA was confirmed in every one of the 47 organ samples, which the page does not state.
websearch.notes: No result link was the study itself (all news/secondary); technologynetworks and thewaternetwork pages unusable (<2000 chars). Also: the closing line that the 2020 quote still reflects current research is unsupported (C); colon cancer tissue finding (higher in tumoral tissue) and urine finding omitted (A); placenta/artery claims come from a Guardian reprint without attribution (D).

webfetch.fetch_prompt: What do the studies described on this page report about microplastics found in human tissues or organs (for example blood, placenta, lung, liver, brain, or feces)? Include the tissues, detection methods, reported particle counts or concentrations, sample sizes, and any health associations or limitations the authors mention.
webfetch.notes: Nature URL gave a 303/302 cookie redirect loop twice (H2 attempts on nature.com and idp.nature.com), so used the PMC copy of the same paper (Nihart et al. 2025). PMC pagetext.py returned only 165 chars, so ground truth fetch.raw.txt is the nature.com page text of the same article (41715 chars). Spot-checked numbers (433/404, 3345/4917, 26,076, 7-30x, 84-96 vs 2-4 months, ~50%, associative caveat) all match.
